sec: The α-intercalated cell and net acid secretion · p822

items.q: The cortical collecting system diagram is drawn for which cell type?
items.exp: The diagram is labelled ‘α intercalated cell’, the acid-secreting cell of the cortical collecting system. (Book p822)

items.q: Match the pumps on the α-intercalated cell — 1) Luminal H⁺ pump  2) Apical exchange pump  3) Which ion is exchanged … A) K⁺  B) H⁺-ATPase  C) H⁺,K⁺-ATPase
items.exp: Both an H⁺-ATPase and an H⁺,K⁺-ATPase are drawn on the luminal side of the α-intercalated cell, the latter exchanging H⁺ for K⁺. (Book p822)

items.q: How many ATP-requiring pumps are labelled in the α-intercalated cell diagram?
items.exp: The diagram labels two ATP-dependent transporters: the H⁺-ATPase and the H⁺,K⁺-ATPase. (Book p822)

items.q: Fill up: Inside the α-intercalated cell, CO₂ + H₂O combine under the influence of ______ to form H₂CO₃.
items.exp: The α-intercalated cell uses CA II to make H₂CO₃ from CO₂ and H₂O; the H⁺ so generated is secreted into the lumen. (Book p822)

items.q: Match the urinary acid species — 1) HPO₄²⁻ → H₂PO₄⁻  2) NH₃ → NH₄⁺  3) Difference between them … A) Non-titratable acid  B) Titratable acid  C) Only the first appears on the titratable-acid line
items.exp: The diagram labels HPO₄²⁻ → H₂PO₄⁻ as titratable acid and NH₃ → NH₄⁺ as non-titratable acid. (Book p822)

items.q: Fill up: Net acid secretion = urine NH₄⁺ + ______ − urine HCO₃⁻.
items.exp: Net acid secretion: urine NH₄⁺ + urine titratable acid − urine HCO₃⁻. (Book p822)

items.q: In the α-intercalated cell diagram, the K⁺ drawn on the luminal side moves:
opts: Into the lumen, exchanged for H⁺ by the H⁺,K⁺-ATPase
Into the cell, exchanged for Na⁺
Into the lumen, pumped by the H⁺-ATPase
Nowhere — K⁺ is shown only intracellularly
items.exp: The H⁺,K⁺-ATPase exchanges H⁺ (secreted) for K⁺ (reabsorbed); K⁺ is also shown exiting to the lumen alongside H⁺ in the diagram. (Book p822)

items.q: ‘The urinary ammonium and phosphate species are both counted as titratable acid in the printed formula.’
opts: False — NH₄⁺ is non-titratable acid; only the phosphate species is titratable acid
True — both are titratable acid by definition
False — HPO₄²⁻ is the non-titratable species
True, but only when urine HCO₃⁻ is zero
items.exp: The diagram labels H₂PO₄⁻ (from HPO₄²⁻) as titratable acid and NH₄⁺ as non-titratable acid; the net acid formula adds both to urine NH₄⁺ and subtracts urine HCO₃⁻. (Book p822)

items.q: All but one of these are labelled on the α-intercalated cell diagram. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: The luminal membrane shows the H⁺-ATPase and the H⁺,K⁺-ATPase with CA II in the cytoplasm; no luminal Na⁺–K⁺-ATPase is drawn. (Book p822)

items.q: A patient's urine shows abundant NH₄⁺ and H₂PO₄⁻ but no HCO₃⁻. What is the net acid secretion according to the printed formula?
opts: Urine NH₄⁺ + urine titratable acid (urine HCO₃⁻ contributes nothing)
Zero, because urine HCO₃⁻ is nil
items.exp: Net acid secretion = urine NH₄⁺ + urine titratable acid − urine HCO₃⁻; with no urinary HCO₃⁻, the two acid species alone determine net acid secretion. (Book p822)
